state$

The state$ stream emits notifications whenever a FeatureCell commits a new state snapshot. It provides a reactive, observable view of state changes, including metadata describing where and why the change occurred.

Stream Contract Summary

  • Emits on every committed state change
  • Includes the full immutable state snapshot
  • Includes optional metadata associated with the update
  • Includes the pipeline stage that originated the change
  • Completes when the FeatureCell is destroyed

The state$ stream is the primary mechanism for reactive state observation. It does not influence pipeline execution, does not control scheduling, and does not participate in state computation. Its sole responsibility is to emit committed state transitions.

Note

All emissions from state$ represent fully committed, immutable state. Subscribers must treat emitted values as read-only.

Configuration
State Stream
Member Description
state$

type:

  • Observable<StateEmitSnapshotShape<T>>

lifecycle:

  • Emits until FeatureCell destruction
Emits a structured snapshot each time the FeatureCell commits state. Includes the immutable state snapshot, optional update metadata, and the pipeline origin of the change.
State Emission Shape

Each emission from state$ is a structured object that describes both the resulting state and the context in which the state change occurred.

State Emit Types

The type field indicates the origin of the state emission within the FeatureCell lifecycle or pipeline.

StateEmitType
Type Description
Incoming Indicates that a new state value entered the pipeline and began processing.
Finalize Indicates that a state value was finalized and successfully committed.
Error Indicates that a state emission occurred as part of error handling.
Reset Indicates that the FeatureCell was reset and its state cleared.
Destroy Indicates that the FeatureCell was destroyed and its lifecycle terminated.

These values are informational and observational only. They do not influence pipeline behavior and must not be relied upon for control flow.

Example

The state$ observable is typically used for reactive subscriptions, side effects, integration with external systems, or advanced coordination logic that depends on state transitions.

Example: Subscribing to FeatureCell State Changes

{{`this.vault.state$
  .subscribe(({ snapshot, type, options }) => {
    console.info('State value:', snapshot.value);
    console.info('Origin type:', type);
    console.info('Options:', options);
  });`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.state$
  .subscribe(({ snapshot, type, options }) => {
    console.info('State value:', snapshot.value);
    console.info('Origin type:', type);
    console.info('Options:', options);
  });`}}

What this does

  • Subscribes to all committed state updates
  • Receives the full immutable state snapshot
  • Receives the pipeline origin of the change
  • Receives optional metadata associated with the update

This pattern is ideal for analytics, logging, debugging, cross-feature coordination, or external integrations that must react to state changes over time.
